rubric_notes: Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Frames the relationship almost entirely at fold a.22 ('superfamily/fold relatives', 'same SCOPe fold'), never names superfamily a.22.1 or release 2.08, gives no family SCCS, and omits the bacterial histone-fold family a.22.1.4. Correctly separates archaeal histones and TAF/NF-Y from the core-histone family and warns against inferring transcriptional roles, but says function can be transferred 'at the broad DNA-wrapping histone-fold level' and that superfamily/fold relatives are valid templates for dimerization geometry, which transfers function/template from fold placement. Confuses the family/superfamily/fold distinction that is central here. No evidence bundle; support is sparse.

Correct inference: superfamily-level remote homology, different families, rejects transferring HisE PRA-PH or MazG specificity either way, names needed external evidence. However it never states the actual SCOPe classifications: no a.204.1.2, a.204.1.4, or a.204.1 identifiers, no SUNIDs, no release; superfamily is described only loosely as a 'MazG/HisE-like nucleotide-pyrophosphohydrolase lineage'. Must_include items 1 and 2 are therefore not met on evidence. No fabrication. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly frames superfamily placement as probable common ancestry stronger than same-fold similarity, names the three families as distinct, and rejects transfer of substrate, polymerization/chaperone roles, oligomeric state, and loop/active-site detail. However it supplies no SCOPe identifiers at all: neither the family SCCS (c.55.1.1, c.55.1.3, c.55.1.4) nor the superfamily c.55.1 nor fold c.55 are stated, and no evidence bundle supports the classifications. Material identifiers required by must_include are missing, so factual support is partial.

Correctly identifies a.25.1.1, a.25.1.2, a.25.1.3 as families within superfamily a.25.1, interprets this as ancient divergence from a common metal-site scaffold, and refuses to transfer iron storage, tyrosyl-radical, or peroxide chemistry from a ferritin template. Concise but omits sequence-level and experimental/biochemical evidence as requirements (only active-site/metal-ligand evidence named) and gives no release, SUNIDs, or SCOPe annotation support (empty bundle). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Never gives the family SCCS codes or states clearly that all three families sit in the same superfamily b.6.1; describes the relationship as 'at most remote-superfamily homology' and frames the caveat as 'just because SCOPe puts them in the cupredoxin-like fold', blurring the fold-versus-superfamily distinction that is central here. Also misnames the superfamily as 'Cupredoxin-like' (that is the fold). Function-transfer caveat (type-1 copper ligands, redox context) is sound and no unsafe transfer. No identifiers, SUNIDs, release, or annotations; empty evidence bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct central inference: distinct families within superfamily d.15.1 supporting remote homology of the beta-grasp scaffold with divergent functions; rejects transferring ubiquitin-conjugation to RBD/UBX and Ras-binding to ubiquitin-related/UBX. However, it never gives the family identifiers d.15.1.1, d.15.1.2, d.15.1.5 required by must_include, names no release, and supplies no supporting evidence. Mentions UBX in the p97/VCP system descriptively but does not explicitly reject p97-binding transfer. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Gives the correct central inference (remote homologs at CheY-like superfamily level within Flavodoxin-like fold, not one interchangeable functional family) and rejects all four named transfers: phosphorelay to ODC wing, PLP decarboxylase to KaiA, and ODC activity or KaiA circadian regulation to arbitrary superfamily members. However no family SCCS codes (c.23.1.1/c.23.1.4/c.23.1.5), no superfamily code c.23.1, no SUNIDs, no release, and empty evidence bundle; domain recruitment and the KaiA receiver-feature caveat are not developed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Gets the general idea (own superfamily within barrel-sandwich-hybrid fold, homology inferred within superfamily, fold alone does not transfer ancestry or function) but provides no identifiers (no b.84, b.84.5, b.84.5.1, no sibling superfamilies), never mentions the family level, and misdescribes the all-beta b.84 architecture as a 'beta-barrel/alpha-beta sandwich'. No evidence bundle. must_include items 1 and 3 unmet; family-versus-superfamily focus not addressed.

Names fold f.21 and superfamilies f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3 correctly (f.21.3 label drops the '1' in 'nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain', minor) and correctly rejects merging and cross-group function/template transfer. No release, SUNIDs, or API evidence supplied (empty bundle), so support is thin though not wrong. Does not state what independent evidence (sequence, structural detail, motifs, biological context) would be needed for a homology claim. Phrase 'structural analogy' is used loosely but not as an absolute non-homology assertion. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Biological interpretation is sound: shared c.2.1 superfamily read as ancient homologous Rossmann core, family split treated as a warning against transferring catalytic residues, oligomeric contacts, substrate specificity and oxidoreductase function, with ADH domains usable only as very remote templates. However the answer never gives the family identifiers c.2.1.1, c.2.1.8, c.2.1.9 or any SUNIDs or release, which the must_include criterion names, and supplies no evidence bundle; hierarchy claims for c.2/c.2.1 and class are correct but sparse. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly answers no and frames the pair as an artificial/design grouping that does not imply natural homology, but never states that both sit in the same k.40.1.1 Designed trimeric coiled-coil family, never cites family SUNID 100905, and never mentions the explicit 'not a true family' annotation that is the decisive caveat. Hard ceiling for ignoring a decisive annotation applies (bio <= 2). Factual support is sparse: no SCCS, SUNID, or annotation evidence; empty evidence bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Claims the current placement is a fold-level merge into c.124 NagB/RpiA/CoA-transferase-like; actual 2.08 placement is c.23.14.2 under Flavodoxin-like fold c.23 and N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like superfamily c.23.14. Uses historical d1t1ja_ as the current SID (must_avoid violation). Gives no SCCS codes for 1.69 and no superfamily-level comparison, so misses the key remote-homology hypothesis and frames the change as fold-only similarity. No evidence bundle. Hard ceilings: wrong relationship-bearing classification and fabricated release-specific placement.

Biological inference is complete: tag is an engineered N-terminal artifact in SCOPe's artifact class, similarity is tag similarity only, not homology, and should be filtered from function/template/representative use. Boundaries (1-8, domain from residue 9) correct. However, it never gives the class letter l, SCCS l.1.1.1, or the N-terminal Tags/Synthetic placement required by must_include, and supplies no supporting evidence; one material identifier missing. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

States the 1.75 whole-chain d1acca_ unit, the later two-SID split, and correctly limits transfer to the matching module with per-domain searching, so the central inference is present. Support is sparse: no SCCS for 1.75 or either current domain, no residue boundaries, no release in which the split appeared or persisted, and the new SIDs are offered only as 'conventional'.

Mosaic concept and transfer caveat present, but module list is wrong: omits the bromodomain (d3jb9a4 a.29.2.1) and substitutes a 'Jab1/MPN metalloprotease-like' domain that is not among the five SCOPe 3jb9 domains. No SIDs, boundaries, SCCS, or identification of the new fold as the N-terminal A:47-697 d.394 domain. Wrong relationship-bearing classification caps reasoning at 2. Evaluator: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct central reasoning: repeat proteins, family reflects homologous repeat unit, length reflects copy number, rejects fixed length and function transfer. Gives correct SCCS levels but no node names, protein/species placements, re heterogeneity annotation, or representative repeat unit, so the annotation-interpretation requirement is unmet and evidence is thin.

Correctly distinguishes stable 2.08 from a date-stamped periodic update, advises pinning 2.08 unless an explicitly named periodic snapshot was used, and says the periodic refresh covers newer PDB entries without redefining the stable classification. Fails to report the concrete periodic label reported by the endpoint and supplies no evidence bundle, so the requested release metadata is incomplete. Calling periodic classifications 'provisional' is imprecise. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Recognizes fragment bias and the value of the complete 1dn1B domain but misdescribes the structures: calls 1br0/1ez3 'short helical pieces' of an Habc three-helix bundle supposedly completed in 1dn1B, whereas SCOPe annotates them as three-helical fragments of a larger (STAT-like four-helix) domain. No SIDs, no a.47.2.1 family, no ms caveat, no evidence bundle. Confuses the fragment/complete-domain relationship it is asked to interpret. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly places c.2/c.2.1 as the Rossmann lineage, distinguishes family (close homologs) from superfamily (remote homologs) from fold, and explains why cofactor geometry and glycine-rich motifs can recur without ancestry. Defaults cross-fold/cross-superfamily NAD(P) binders to 'independent, convergent solutions' with only a brief 'unless stronger structural evidence' hedge, and the evidence-integration list is thin (global fold agreement plus SCOPe placement; no sequence, motif-in-context, or phylogenetic evidence). Facts stated are correct but sparse: only one fold named, no release, no other NAD(P)-binding superfamilies identified. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Misidentifies the compared Cry3A domain throughout as d1dlca3, which is the N-terminal delta-endotoxin domain (f.1.3.1, A:61-289), not the C-terminal b.18.1.3 beta-sandwich at A:500-644, and then recommends using that wrong domain for the comparison and template scoping. Supplies no superfamily or family codes, no release labels, and no identifiers for the 2.04 versus 2.08 states, so the required before/after comparison is asserted rather than evidenced. The general conclusion (class-level separation promoted to superfamily, families still distinct, no function transfer) is correct, which keeps one element intact. Eval: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Hierarchy is correct and family-level homology is retained, but the hf annotation is misread: the answer treats hf as meaning the entry has heterogeneous segments outside a comparable homeodomain core ('every attached segment, or the whole PDB chain'), and says the two can be compared 'over the curated homeodomain portion'. SCOPe hf means the domain itself adopts a different fold than the exemplar despite similar sequence and secondary-structure count, so the answer implicitly assumes identical core geometry (must_avoid) and never states the actual caveat. d1ztra1 is 1ztr A:0-59, essentially the whole chain, so the 'heterogeneous part' framing is unsupported. No release, SUNIDs, boundaries, or hf definition given; no evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Reasoning correct at a general level: fragment is a coverage warning not a family change, align only over present core, prefer complete d1uc6a1 as template/representative, use fragment only when partial acceptable, do not count as distinct architecture or transfer function beyond aligned region. Omits explicit score-comparability statement and labeling/coverage retention. Factual support sparse: no release, no boundaries, no fr definition or SUNIDs, no evidence bundle; stated hierarchy is correct. Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Defines fold (may reflect homology or analogy), superfamily (probable common origin from structural/functional/biological evidence), and family (closer homology), then states the claim of each of the three placements explicitly and picks new superfamily. Rejects function/annotation transfer from fold match and names the independent evidence required, treating fold-level templates as topology-guided only. No identifiers; no factual errors. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Reasoning is complete: superfamily d.144.1 membership supports a homologous bilobal catalytic core and broad ATP/Mg-dependent phosphotransfer, but not acceptor substrate or regulation; states substrate classes are separate family-level specializations and lists family/orthology sequence evidence, substrate-contact residue conservation, ligand-bound structures, accessory-domain architecture, and biochemical assays. Factual support is thinner: the three family identifiers (d.144.1.7, d.144.1.6, d.144.1.4) required by the gold criteria are never given, and no evidence bundle backs the classifications; fold and superfamily SCCS are correct.
